headline: Boston woman identified after SUV crashes into Faulkner Hospital campus
dek: Patricia McGrath, 68, died after the Oct. 1 collision in Jamaica Plain; authorities say the crash remains under investigation and no criminal charges have been filed.
body: Patricia McGrath, a 68-year-old Dorchester resident, has been identified as the woman who died after an SUV struck her outside Brigham and Women’s Faulkner Hospital in Jamaica Plain, according to the [Suffolk County District Attorney’s Office, as reported by WHDH 7News](https://whdh.com/news/woman-killed-when-car-slammed-into-hospital-building-in-jamaica-plain-identified/). The crash happened Thursday, Oct. 1, near the hospital’s dialysis unit, where Boston police said McGrath was sitting on a bench.

The vehicle continued from the pedestrian area into the hospital campus and hit the wall of the Belkin House, a separate building at the Faulkner complex, around 10:45 a.m. The collision damaged a gas line. McGrath was taken for treatment and later died, while two people who were inside the SUV were also injured and brought to the hospital, [CBS Boston reported](https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/3-injured-car-crash-faulkner-hospital/). The available reports do not identify the two occupants or describe the severity of their injuries beyond their transport for medical care.

The damaged gas line turned the crash into a wider campus safety response. Faulkner Hospital said the Belkin House was evacuated as a precaution while crews worked with National Grid and the Boston Fire Department. The main hospital building was reported safe and operating at the time, and National Grid shut off gas service to the rest of the hospital after the collision. Four Boston EMS members were also evaluated for possible gas exposure, CBS Boston said.

The incident temporarily affected the area around the medical campus. Emergency responders and the damaged building created traffic impacts, according to the hospital statement cited by CBS. That matters in Jamaica Plain because Faulkner serves southwest Boston and nearby suburbs as a community teaching hospital, and the crash occurred beside a facility that was continuing to provide care while the scene was secured. The reports do not establish how long the Belkin House evacuation lasted or whether the building sustained damage beyond the gas-line impact.

Authorities have described the collision as an accident rather than a deliberate act. Boston police sent homicide detectives and the department’s fatal-collision team to the scene, a response that reflects the death and the need to reconstruct what happened, not a public finding that a crime occurred. As of the victim-identification update on Oct. 2, the district attorney’s office said no criminal charges had been filed. The investigation remained open.

The public record still leaves key questions unanswered. None of the cited reports explains why the SUV left its path, whether a medical emergency or a vehicle problem played a role, or whether investigators have identified any contributing roadway or campus conditions. Those questions should not be filled with speculation. The early police description and the prosecutor’s update establish the result of the crash, but they do not assign fault or provide a final account of the driver’s actions.

The sequence also illustrates why a collision near a hospital can affect more people than those directly involved. A pedestrian was killed, the vehicle occupants needed care, emergency workers were assessed for exposure, a campus building was cleared, and utility crews had to isolate a damaged gas line while the main hospital remained open. Each part of that response was reported by officials or hospital representatives through local news coverage; NorthEast News did not witness the crash or independently inspect the scene.

For now, the confirmed update is McGrath’s identity and the status of the case, not a final explanation of the crash. Boston police and the Suffolk County District Attorney’s Office have not announced charges in the reports reviewed for this article. Further information about the investigation, the injured occupants, the gas-line repair or the Belkin House’s operating status would need to come from those agencies or the hospital. Until then, the Oct. 1 collision remains a fatal crash under investigation on the Faulkner Hospital campus.
